0.content: Crepus Ragnvindr, the former master of the Dawn Winery, was Diluc's father. He had wanted to be a knight and failed to qualify, and he never received a Vision, so he hoped his son would become the most esteemed knight of all and taught him that the world would never turn its back on the faithful. On Diluc's eighteenth birthday (after a coming-of-age celebration at Angel's Share, in the manga), a monster attacked the transport fleet carrying father and son. Crepus repelled it with an "unknown evil power", a Delusion, which then backfired and mortally wounded him. In Diluc's account Crepus died in his son's arms. He also took in Kaeya and raised him as a son. Crepus's employees, Elzer among them, mourned him.

1.content: Kaeya Alberich is Crepus's adopted son and the current Cavalry Captain, the post Diluc once held. As young men they were Mondstadt's most eye-catching pair, almost like twins, protecting the city "in both light and dark". When Crepus died, Kaeya arrived too late, and in shock he smirked that the world was "truly... fascinating". That night, consumed by guilt, Kaeya told Diluc the truth: he was an agent of Khaenri'ah left in Mondstadt by his birth father. The brothers fought, and Kaeya's Cryo Vision awoke in the clash. It has been a long time since Kaeya called Diluc "brother".

2.content: After his return, an unknown guardian began working at night. Monsters were found dead in the wilds, wanted thieves turned up hanging bound in the statue plaza, and an Abyss Mage the Knights hunted was found already dead. A smell of burning and a flash of red flame were all anyone saw. Tavern talk named him the "Darknight Hero". Diluc publicly scorns the name. Elzer is one of the few who know. In his Story Quest (1.0) the Traveler caught him killing an Abyss Mage. When the Abyss Order sent a challenge, he interrogated a mage named Landrich for the attack plan, lured a slime horde with experimental bait as a diversion, shamed the watching knight Huffman into leaving his post, wiped out the horde and was back behind the bar with his "patrons" (winery staff) as his alibi. Kaeya saw through it and kept quiet.

3.comment: Diluc: Dawn Winery and Angel's Share
3.content: The Dawn Winery is Mondstadt's chief winery, owned by the Ragnvindr Clan for about a thousand years. It is famous for Dandelion Wine. It controls roughly half of Mondstadt's wine trade and owns Angel's Share, the city's best-known tavern and centre of information, where Charles tends bar and Diluc sometimes takes over. The motto on its plaque is "Shine True". Diluc introduced alcohol-free drinks such as apple cider and keeps grape juice stocked.

4.comment: Diluc: The Knights of Favonius and Eroch
4.content: Diluc passed the Knights' trials and rose to become the youngest Cavalry Captain in their history. After his father's death, Inspector Eroch ordered him to "conceal the truth" and present it as an accident to protect the Knights' reputation. Diluc did not even argue. He resigned that day and left his Vision behind. Within the four years he was away, Eroch was exposed as a traitor and purged. Diluc still criticises the Knights as slow and inefficient, but he respects individuals.

5.comment: Diluc: Northern Intelligence Network and Nefer
5.content: While hunting the Fatui, Diluc drew the Harbingers' attention and barely escaped death. He was saved by an observer from a vast underground intelligence network in the north, who had been watching him and approved of his methods. He joined and rose into its upper ranks. Its members are volunteers who often give up their status and even their names. The network is run by Nefer from the Curatorium of Secrets in Nod-Krai. She calls him "Owl", names him a key Mondstadt informant, and says working with him is a pleasure because "he pays promptly".
